newsitem.title: FRANCE: POLL - Most French favour cap on family allowances.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Most French favour cap on family allowances.

text.p: Most French people favour a controversial plan by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to withdraw generous family allowances from the better off, according to an opinion poll made public on Wednesday.
The Ipsos poll for the weekly L'Evenement du Jeudi found that 62 percent believed the plan was fair and helped advance social unity while 34 percent said it did not.
Four percent offered no opinion in the survey of 956 people aged 18 and above, conducted on June 27-28.

Jospin's leftist government, in power just one month, has insisted it would not back down on the plan to curb family allowances to households earning comfortable incomes so that limited resources could be shifted to the poor.
The proposal, widely viewed as a first test of the new government's resolve, has come under fire from trade unions and family groups and some Communist deputies.
The Communists hold three posts in the cabinet and are part of the Socialist-led majority in parliament which also includes Greens.
